title: HorecaOS — is it working
description: ADR 0023's one dashboard. Panels answer the three 3am questions (is it down, is it losing money, is it losing data) from what /actuator/prometheus actually publishes. Nothing on this page pages anyone; alerting.env's Alertmanager routes do that from prometheus/rules/adr-0023-alerts.yml. The bottom-right panel lists what this page deliberately cannot show.

panels.title: App reachable (on-box scrape)
panels.description: Whether THIS Prometheus's own scrape of the application succeeded. This is not the external uptime check ADR 0023 requires for the night 'platform unreachable' alert — that check watches the platform from outside the box, on purpose, so that it keeps working when this box does not. Treat this panel as a diagnostic, never as proof the platform is reachable from the internet.

panels.title: Outbox oldest pending age
panels.description: Night alert: HorecaosOrderFlowStalled fires at 900s (ADR 0006's relay backs off to at most 5 minutes across 10 attempts, ~13.5 minutes worst case, so nothing healthy reaches 15).

panels.title: Inbox oldest pending age
panels.description: Same alert and threshold as the outbox panel; the two are one night alert with two legs (plus a Kafka consumer-lag leg this dashboard cannot show — see the gaps panel).

panels.title: Oldest live order age
panels.description: Diagnosis, not an alert (ADR 0023 pages on the outbox/inbox age, not on this). Whether a stalled outbox has left a hundred orders sitting in PAYMENT_AUTHORIZING or none.

panels.title: Orders by status (live)
panels.description: horecaos.orders.live — orders that have not reached a terminal status, by status. Nothing here pages; it is the diagnosis after the order-flow alert has already fired.

panels.title: Dead letters by topic domain
panels.description: horecaos.outbox.dead.letters and horecaos.inbox.dead.letters. monetary=true rows are the ones the trading-hours HorecaosMonetaryDeadLetter alert watches; outbox rows are always failure_category="unclassified" — ADR 0023's outbox-has-no-classification-column gap, not a display bug.

panels.title: HTTP requests by outcome
panels.description: Standard Spring Boot request metric, grouped by outcome (SUCCESS/CLIENT_ERROR/SERVER_ERROR/...). ADR 0023 deliberately does not page on a 5xx rate anywhere except the two payment callback roots (see the next panel) — a single request failure here is expected to be on this dashboard and nowhere louder.

panels.title: Payment callback non-2xx rate
panels.description: The one route-specific alert in ADR 0023: more than 3 non-200 responses from /providers/payme/* or /providers/click/* in 5 minutes pages the trading-hours tier (HorecaosPaymentCallbackFailing). Both providers retry any non-200 until the payment reaches their manual investigation queue.

panels.title: Provider circuit state
panels.description: horecaos.provider.circuit.state (0 closed, 1 half open, 2 open, 3 forced/disabled) and how long each has been continuously open. Only payment/pos breakers being open for 10+ minutes page (trading tier); a courier breaker opening is here and nowhere louder, deliberately (ADR 0023).

panels.title: Fenced writes by capability (cutover only)
panels.description: horecaos.migration.writes.fenced. One fenced write is the ADR 0024 ownership gate working correctly; more than 10 in 5 minutes for one capability pages (HorecaosOwnershipFenceBurst) because routing and ownership disagree. Outside a cutover this stays flat at zero.

panels.title: Onboarding stalled age
panels.description: horecaos.onboarding.runs.stalled.age.seconds. Morning-tier alert at 3600s; the gauge's own -1 sentinel means 'could not read the database' and is not an age.

panels.title: Free space, application container's own path (NOT the host)
panels.description: disk_free_bytes / disk_total_bytes for the path this application container sees. DataVolumeMetrics's own documentation is explicit that on the production VM this container's filesystem is read-only and this figure describes nothing about the host's real data volume — the 85% morning alert is evaluated by horecaos-probe.sh reading the actual host with df -P, not from this panel. Shown here only because it is what makes the disk visible in a rehearsal or staging VM where no probe runs.

panels.title: What this dashboard cannot show you

options.content:
Watched by **horecaos-probe.sh** directly against the host or a container, or by an **off-box service** — not visible to this Prometheus because nothing here scrapes anything but the application:

- **Platform unreachable** — the external uptime check (off-box, by design)
- **PostgreSQL down** — `pg_isready` against the database container
- **Kafka consumer lag** — `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe` against the broker
- **OpenBao sealed** — `bao status` against the OpenBao container
- **Backup did not run** — the host's backup stamp file
- **Real host disk %** — `df -P` on the host (see the caption on the disk panel to the left)
- **TLS certificate expiry** — a live TLS handshake against the public hostname
- **Container crash loops** — Docker restart counts via `docker inspect`

See `infra/observability/README.md` and `docs/adr/partial/0023-*.md` for why each stays with the probe instead of being duplicated here.
